summary: The subtype guard is correctly conservative for flange candidates, but it is not scoped to flange queries and can turn ordinary welded-end valve requests into false NOT_FOUND results. The returned selected list also remains inconsistent with the verified final match.
issues: query_flange_subtype() recognizes cues such as «приварной в стык» without first confirming that the query is for a flange. Thus a valid non-flange query such as «Кран шаровой приварной в стык DN80» receives weld_neck as a flange requirement; all ball-valve candidates are then unknown and the matcher abstains. This contradicts the stated preservation of non-flange behavior and is not covered by the tests.

After subtype verification, MatchResult.selected is built from every LLM-selected item rather than the compatible selected_items. A NOT_FOUND response can therefore still expose incompatible selections, while a MATCHED response can expose a rejected flat flange ahead of its accepted weld-neck result. This is misleading to CLI/serialization/evaluation consumers that use selected.
fix_plan: Scope query_flange_subtype() to flange product queries (or apply the guard only when the query product type is flange), then add regression tests for non-flange queries containing weld/butt-weld or collar wording.
Build MatchResult.selected from the post-validation selected_items; return an empty selected list on subtype-caused NOT_FOUND. Extend matcher tests to assert those output invariants.
Re-run focused and full tests, then let the supervisor repeat public evaluation when Qdrant is available.
next_direction: Keep this deterministic affirmative-evidence approach, but enforce subtype semantics only in their product-class context. The supplied public evaluation produced no quality result because Qdrant was unavailable, so the repaired candidate still needs measured comparison.
